purpose: The single declared mapping between the GitHub label taxonomy and config/remediation-plan.json. tests/prod/112 reads ONLY this file to decide what agreement means; no label-to-plan translation is written into shell conditionals.
why: The live half of 112 compared MEMBERSHIP alone — every open issue appears in the plan, no closed issue is listed as active work. It never compared status, so the authenticated backlog lane stayed green while #345 was status:partial live and status ready in the plan. Membership agreement is not semantic agreement, and this file is what makes the difference assertable.

field_mapping.note: exactly one status label is required; the mapping below decides which plan status it means
agrees for 175/175 planned open issues on master 7eb02d21, so it is enforced rather than merely recorded
the plan carries both the short key and the title; the title is what GitHub exposes

non_normative.reason: editorial; the plan deliberately does not mirror issue prose
ownership is not modelled in the plan
not part of the plan schema; a new label prefix must be added here before it can be enforced

status:verified.reason: verified work is CLOSED. The label on an open planned issue is itself drift, so it maps to no plan status rather than being silently accepted.

reconciliation_debt.why: EMPTY, and that is a resolved state, not an unused slot. The one class this list carried -- M4 records where the plan said `ready` and the label said `blocked`, 54 at first and 39 after the M4 scanner-evidence batch merged -- was discharged by #350 on evidence, not by a judgement call. The disagreement was never semantic. Every `status:*` label in this repository was applied in a single bulk pass on 2026-08-06 reflecting the plan state of that day, and the 39 were exactly the records whose plan `blocked_by` was non-empty on that date: 36 blocked by #182, and #123/#124/#128 blocked by #259. Both closed on 2026-08-08 and the plan was reconciled the same day (`33789265`, `70d04415`); the labels never were. The control is exact -- the 7 M4 records carrying an empty `blocked_by` on 2026-08-06 were labelled `ready` and still are, with no exceptions on either side, which is the rule this entry once said no rule explained. So the labels were stale and the plan was authoritative, and the feared alternative -- an incomplete `blocked_by` that would have invalidated the wave ordering -- is REFUTED rather than merely unconfirmed. The mechanism below stays in place, unused: the next drift must still be named before it can be excused.
rules: An entry permits ONE named issue to disagree on ONE named field, and only for the exact (plan_value, live_value) pair recorded.
An entry whose issue no longer disagrees on that field is STALE and fails, so the list can only shrink.
An entry whose observed pair differs from the recorded pair fails, so drift changing shape is not absorbed.
Drift on any (issue, field) not listed here fails. This list is not a policy, it is a named debt.
Every entry carries a machine-readable reason naming a declared class, so distinct debt classes cannot be conflated.

fails_when: the issue is no longer open (debt-not-live)
the issue is no longer in the plan (debt-not-planned)
the field is no longer normative (debt-field-not-normative)
the reason names no declared class (debt-unknown-class)
a declared class has no entries (debt-class-empty) — a discharged class is removed with its last entry, not kept as a slot
review_by is not a real YYYY-MM-DD calendar date (debt-review-by-malformed) — a value the expiry comparison cannot order would never expire, which is the unbounded exception this contract forbids
NOTE: a class carries no `count`. It was derived data that nothing asserted, so it could go stale silently; the entry list is the only source.
entry_contract.why: Debt must not behave as a permanent allowlist. Every failure mode above turns an entry from an exception into an error, so an entry survives only while it remains exactly the mismatch it was written for, and only until its review boundary.
